Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This call is being recorded for claim purposes. Can you confirm
you're okay to continue?
A: Yes, that's fine.
Q: Can you describe where you were driving when the collision happened?
A: I was heading down a main road in Pasadena, Texas, in the right lane. Traffic had slowed up ahead because of a
light that had turned red.
Q: What happened next?
A: I came to a stop behind a car at the light. About a few seconds later, I felt a hard jolt from behind. My head
snapped forward and then back against the seat.
Q: Did you see the vehicle that hit you before the impact?
A: No, I didn't. I was looking at the light and the car in front of me. I only noticed it when I heard the brakes squeal and
then the impact.
Q: Did you get out of your vehicle at the scene?
A: I did, but my left knee gave out when I stepped down. It struck the door frame and I had to hold onto the car to stay
upright.
Q: Have you sought medical treatment for your knee?
A: Yes. I was taken to an urgent care cilnic that same afternoon. They took X-rays and said there was swelling and
some ligament soreness. I've been told to keep weight off it for a while and to follow up with an orthopedic doctor.
Q: Is there anything else about the accident you'd like to add?
A: Only that my car has damage to the rear bumper and trunk, and I'm still having trouble walking up stairs. I'll send
over the clinic paperwork when I get home.
Q: Thank you. We'll follow up with you once we've reviewed everything.
A: Thanks, I appreciate it.
</page>

injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
